items.title: The Many Open Questions About the Trump Administration’s New De Facto AI Model Licensing System
items.excerpt: Adam Conner (Center for American Progress) argues the confidential AI framework created under the June 2026 executive order works as a de facto licensing system for frontier models, with no public answer on which models are covered or who gets early access. He notes the government has agreed to release the framework text by Oct. 30.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us
items.excerpt: AI company leaders joined whistleblowers and security officials at a broad UK parliamentary session and asked lawmakers for regulation. Nearby, Britain’s spy chief warned that AI could be used to create new bioweapons.

items.title: MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
items.excerpt: MI5 has launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre to help Britain respond to AI-enabled state threats, terrorism and bioweapons.

items.title: Lights, bells and liability: Europe’s privacy regulators crack down on smart glasses
items.excerpt: Under EU privacy law, makers of AI smart glasses could be required to build in flashing lights and audio alerts that show when the glasses are recording.

items.title: Home Office asylum AI flunks one in five accuracy checks
items.excerpt: Ministers promised the UK Home Office's AI tools would speed up asylum decisions. Campaigners say the technology fails one in five accuracy checks, and processing times are getting longer.

items.title: Saudi National Arrested for Installing Surreptitious Audio Recording Device at OpenAI
items.excerpt: DOJ says an OpenAI employee, a Saudi national, was arrested and charged with using or trying to use a device to intercept oral communications after a recording device was found hidden in an OpenAI conference room in San Francisco. (Same story as The Verge: theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1010642)

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly wanted control over what safety reviewers can publish.
items.excerpt: Citing a Reuters report, The Verge says OpenAI and Anthropic considered tighter restrictions on what third-party safety evaluators can publish, because they were worried about trade-secret leaks.

items.title: The US government launched a “Super Intelligence” website.
items.excerpt: The administration launched si.gov as the “official home of America’s work to lead the world in Super Intelligence,” after the White House moved to rename AI as “super intelligence.”

items.title: More than 400 researchers call for stronger AI testing safeguards.
items.excerpt: In an open letter, more than 400 researchers raise concerns about a wave of rogue AI hacks on third-party companies and ask AI companies to adopt high-assurance containment standards for testing.

items.title: The Biggest Pro-AI Super PAC Network Has Poured Millions Into Nevada Shell Companies
items.excerpt: Leading the Future, a super PAC network backed by Silicon Valley figures, has raised large sums to support pro-AI candidates in both parties and has routed millions through Nevada shell companies, WIRED reports.

items.title: These Midterm Races Will Decide Data Centers’ Political Fate
items.excerpt: In Senate, House and governor races across the US, candidates are competing to look the most opposed to AI data centers ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms.

items.title: (LEAD) Arms agency to accelerate development of nuclear-powered subs, AI-driven combat systems
items.excerpt: South Korea's Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) told lawmakers it will speed up development of nuclear-powered submarines and AI-driven combat systems. This is a procurement-policy step beyond the Pangyo AX hub opening.

items.title: 반도체·차 공정에 휴머노이드 20대 투입…규제 풀고 현장 실증
items.excerpt: 정부가 관련 규제를 풀어 반도체·자동차·조선 등 주력 제조업 생산 라인에 이동형 휴머노이드 로봇 20대를 시범 투입하고 현장 실증을 진행한다. 피지컬 AI 정책의 일환이다.

items.title: 진보당 "대전시 인공지능 조례, '브레이크' 없는 반쪽짜리"
items.excerpt: 대전시가 지난달 입법예고한 '대전광역시 인공지능(AI) 기본 조례안'을 두고 진보당 대전시당은 13일 논평을 내고 위험 관리 장치('브레이크')가 없는 반쪽짜리 조례라고 비판했다.

items.title: The UAE embraces AI for kindergartners
items.excerpt: The UAE now requires AI education from kindergarten through 12th grade. Rest of World looks at what schooling could look like if national policy treats AI literacy as basic as reading and writing.

items.title: Shaping global governance of AI agents
items.excerpt: Landry Signé and Karla Yee Amezaga explain how AI agents strain existing governance models and describe what practical oversight could look like.

items.title: AI Governance Needs an Internet-Style Network, Not a Global Overseer
items.excerpt: Konstantinos Komaitis argues that global AI governance should be a distributed network of connected expertise that can challenge governments and companies, rather than a single global overseer.

items.title: Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs in a single year, report claims
items.excerpt: A report says Chinese AI firms bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs this year, chips that fall under US export-control limits, to fill a compute shortage. The same report says Huawei's share of China's AI-chip market is rising. (Off-list source: no on-list outlet had a fresh chip-export item.)
